newsitem.title: UK: Fitch sees AAA for Univ.Support asset-backed notes.
newsitem.headline: Fitch sees AAA for Univ.Support asset-backed notes.

text.p: Fitch Investors Service said on Wednesday it expected to assign an AAA rating to University Support Services Inc's $204.3 million education loan asset-backed notes, series 1996A.
Additionally, the $31.7 million subordinated series 1996B are expected to be rated A, Fitch said.

"The ratings of the notes are based on the legal structure, the quality of the collateral, the enhancement to the collateral provided by nine surety bonds underwritten by St Paul Fire and Marine Insurance Co, the quality of the origination and servicing of the loans by Norwest Bank South Dakota, N.A. and the ability to pass stressful cash flow tests at each rating level," Fitch said in a statement.

"The AAA rating is also based on the 13.4 percent subordination level provided by the subordinated notes and the reserve fund, initially sized at $4.7 million, or the greater of $1.0 million or 2.0 percent of notes outstanding after May 20, 1997," the agency said.

"The A rating is also based on the reserve fund. The note proceeds were used to acquire approximately $220 million of student loans, fund the reserve fund with $4.7 million, pay surety premiums of $2.3 million, fund $5.3 million for working capital for University Support Services (USS), lend moneys to Servus Financial Corp (an affiliate integrally involved in the USS student loan business), pay costs of issuance and fund various accounts provided for in the indenture," Fitch said.
It said the collateral securing the notes included unsecured supplemental student loans, the security for which was enhanced by surety bonds provided by St Paul Fire and Marine.

"The student loans are not Federal Family Education Loan Programme loans and are not guaranteed by a designated guarantor nor reinsured by the U.S. Department of Education," said Fitch. "The loans are indexed to the maximum of 30-day or 90-day commercial paper or the prime rate. The senior and subordinated notes interest rates are taxable securities and are indexed to the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate."
Fitch said interest on the senior series 1996A and subordinated series 1996B is paid monthly starting December 20, 1996.

"The senior and subordinated notes are subject to optional, mandatory and extraordinary redemptions. All principal of the senior notes must be paid prior to the payment of any subordinated notes," the agency said.
The final maturity date for both classes of debt is October 20, 2011, said Fitch.
